World.title: Heavy rain and wind may cause power outages over the weekend
World.content:
Environment Agency forecasts heavy rain, thunderstorms and wind gusts up to 20 meters per second over the weekend and at the start of next week. More difficult weather conditions may lead to trees and branches breaking and cause power outages, grid operator Elektrilevi warns.

On Saturday afternoon and evening, heavy rainfall will spread across Estonia, with thunderstorms in places and wind strengthening in many areas with gusts of 15–20 meters per second. On Sunday, the risk of heavy rain and thunderstorms remains in many places, and rainy weather will continue at the beginning of next week.

Heavy rain and wind gusts may break trees and branches and cause power outages in some areas.

"Elektrilevi is closely monitoring the weekend weather conditions, and our control center and volunteer crisis reserve are ready to respond to possible faults with increased capacity. We recommend people stay indoors when the weather worsens, charge phones and power banks in advance, and stock up on necessary drinking water and food at home," said Elektrilevi board chairman Mihkel Härm.

More detailed guidance can be found in the power outage instructions on Olevalmis.ee.

During heavy rain, thunderstorms and strong winds, stay indoors if possible and keep pets inside as well. Avoid unnecessary driving. If driving is unavoidable, choose a speed suitable for the weather conditions and be aware of trees, branches and other obstacles that may fall onto the road. Stay away from fallen power lines and report them to Elektrilevi's fault line at 1343. During thunderstorms, avoid open areas and stay away from bodies of water and isolated tall trees. In a power outage, use a battery‑powered flashlight as a light source, not candles.

Elektrilevi asks that all power outages be reported through the MARU app. This allows fast information exchange between the customer and Elektrilevi during electrical faults.

Current information on the number and locations of outages can be followed on Elektrilevi's outage map.

World.title: Estonia pushes 112 accessibility deadline to 2027 as service falls short
World.content:
Many still face barriers using Estonia's 112 emergency line, including deaf people and those unable to speak safely in an emergency, as full accessibility is pushed to 2027.

While Estonia was supposed to meet accessibility requirements by June 2025, the necessary systems still aren't fully in place. Currently, people can contact the Emergency Response Center by voice call or SMS, but neither option works equally for everyone.

For example, deaf or hard of hearing people, as well as those who have had a stroke, whose speech is impaired or who cannot safely speak in an emergency may need alternatives such as video calls or real-time text (RTT).

Mari Tuulik, an accessibility advocate with the Estonian Chamber of Disabled People (EPIKoda), said SMS service doesn't ensure access for everyone, including those with difficulty reading or writing.

"This also affects deaf people who use Estonian Sign Language (EVK) but for whom Estonian is essentially a foreign language," Tuulik said, noting that sign languages have their own grammar and vocabulary.

"In time-critical situations, the most accessible option for deaf people would be for at least some emergency dispatchers to know EVK well enough to communicate," she added. "That would be the best option."

'They had three years to get this done'

Accessibility requirements for emergency lines took effect June 28, 2025. Because Estonia's emergency line does not yet meet them, however, the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications plans to invoke an exception allowed under EU rules and move the deadline to June 28, 2027.

Accessibility expert Jakob Rosin said the work should have started sooner.

Emergency dispatchers at an Emergency Response Center in Estonia. Source: ERR

"I've actually seen no good reason why this is taking so long," Rosin said, adding that state agencies didn't only learn about the need for accessibility improvements last year.

Estonia's accessibility legislation took effect in 2022 already, he added, "so there were at least three years to get this done."

The Emergency Response Center is testing new technology, including RTT. Unlike with SMS, or regular text messages, real-time text would allow the emergency dispatcher to see the caller's text as it is being typed.

A video solution is also still in the works, as options offered by phone manufacturers do not meet all users' needs.

SMS still best option for now

Sirli Seegar, the center's social affairs expert, said the goal is to combine multiple forms of communication in a single 112 call.

"Our long-term goal is to offer a complete conversation during a 112 call," Seegar said. "This would mean that the caller and emergency dispatcher could speak, type in real time and share video all during the same call."

She said RTT should be ready to roll out by next June, with officials continuing to work on a video solution. In the meantime, despite follow-up questions and responses taking longer by text, SMS still remains the main option for callers who cannot communicate by voice.

World.title: After five years in office, President Alar Karis has chores waiting at home
World.content:
After five years in Kadriorg, Estonian President Alar and First Lady Sirje Karis are looking ahead to what's next, with plenty of chores to catch up on at home.

"Life has been quite interesting, and I've learned a lot over these five years," said Sirje Karis, speaking at the couple's final Restoration of Independence Day Rose Garden reception as hosts. "I've met many wonderful people, both in Estonia and around the world."

While her husband's term as president is coming to an end, Sirje Karis expects to retain some of her public duties as First Lady after leaving the presidential residence.

"Unfortunately, I can't simply leave all of my responsibilities behind, so some things will remain," she added.

Even so, Sirje Karis said she is looking forward to spending more time around the house in Tartu again.

"I have my own garden and greenhouse," she added. "I love gardening."

DIY or don't

After leaving Kadriorg, the couple will also have to work out how to divide their time between Tallinn and Tartu. "We'll probably spend more of our time in Southern Estonia," Alar Karis said.

The president said he has a growing list of chores and projects waiting to be tackled once he leaves office.

"Our home has become a summer home," he admitted. "You head there and notice the spiderwebs are back again."

"I won't paint ceilings or floors, but I still do a lot of things myself when I can be at home," said Sirje Karis.

Not everything will be a DIY project, however. Karis joked that just a trip to a hardware store can leave even the president overwhelmed by the huge selection.

"You may want to do it yourself, but you simply don't know how," he said. "We've reached the point where if you don't know how to do something yourself, you should leave it to the pros."

Still busy for now

For now, Karis still has little time for home projects. Over the next five weeks, before his presidential term draws to a close, his time in Estonia will be limited by a string of visits abroad.

"In two or three days, I'm off to Ukraine, then Latvia and Italy, and after that it's trips to the Nordic countries, Germany and New York," he said.

The Riigikogu convenes to elect the next president of Estonia on September 2.

World.title: Canadian Estonian KESKfEST marks home stretch for Toronto center build
World.content:
The Canadian Estonian community is already celebrating the long-awaited KESKUS International Estonian Center in Toronto as construction enters its final stretch.

KESKfEST, a multiday public festival in Toronto's Annex neighborhood, was originally planned to mark KESKUS' opening in time for Restoration of Independence Day on August 20.

With construction still underway, the community is instead celebrating the project's nearing completion, or "final countdown."

Events kicked off on Thursday and run through Sunday, featuring speakers and performers from as far as Estonia, film screenings, conferences, Annex neighborhood walking tours, workshops and nightly gatherings, culminating in a folk festival, or valguspidu, with hundreds of choir singers, dancers and gymnasts.

The $56 million — or approximately €35 million — project was initially slated to be completed in 2022, but project manager Ellen Valter said the COVID pandemic, soaring construction costs, supply problems and technical issues repeatedly pushed back the timeline.

Estonian Ambassador to Canada Toomas Lukk (right) at KESKUS groundbreaking ceremony in Toronto on April 8. Source: KESKUS International Estonian Center

"We really are pushing hard now to finish construction so we can celebrate Christmas and New Year's in the newly opened center," Valter said.

KESKUS marks one of the Toronto-area Estonian community's most ambitious projects to date. Funding has come from the sale of the former Toronto Estonian House on Broadview Avenue six years ago, private donations as well as contributions from the Estonian and Canadian governments.

'Now we have a new Estonian House'

Selling the old Estonian House building was an emotional decision for many community members. Although it was far from downtown and increasingly outdated, the building had served as a gathering place and second home for generations of Estonians in Toronto.

Toronto Estonian House chair Veiko Parming said leaving was difficult but necessary.

Photos of the Toronto Estonian House before it was closed and sold. Source: Kerly Ilves

"The old Estonian House was our home for a very long time, including the entire time Estonia was not free," Parming said. "It was the place where everyone who lived here came together."

But the aging building ultimately made a move unavoidable, he acknowledged, "so we had to move forward. And now we have a new Estonian House."

The new KESKUS is designed to bring the area's sizable diaspora community together under one roof at the corner of Bloor Street and Madison Avenue, in the heart of Toronto.

Located next door to Tartu College, another building that has long served the local Estonian community, KESKUS will include a concert hall, library, classrooms, offices and a restaurant.

Organizers also hope the more central and accessible location will attract younger generations and give Estonian cultural life a stronger presence in downtown Toronto.

World.title: Iran president says time to end war while in position of strength
World.content:
Tehran – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Friday it was time to end the months-long Middle East war with the United States because Tehran appeared to be in a stronger position than Washington.

Talks between the decades-old foes remain on hold, with both sides in the war started by the US and Israel in February locked in a stalemate.

Tehran is keeping the key Strait of Hormuz partially shut and Washington is persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran.

“It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity,” Pezeshkian said in a meeting with doctors.

“The whole world acknowledges our victory and emphasises that America has attacked our schools, hospitals and infrastructure in violation of all regulations and is hated around the world.”

Pezeshkian also defended a memorandum of understanding agreed with the US in June aimed at ending the war, claiming it did not signal a defeat for Tehran.

“They cannot find even a single clause in this agreement that indicates capitulation. All the commitments concern the other side,” he said.

His remarks come weeks after Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said he had approved the deal to end the war despite having “different views”.

Hardline lawmakers in Iran’s parliament have also criticised the government over the deal, accusing it of giving concessions to the US, mostly over the re-opening of the strategic Hormuz Strait.

According to reports in US media, the American navy has been organising and protecting secret convoys of tankers through the southern sector of the Strait of Hormuz enabling between five and 10 million barrels a day of oil to be exported.

As Tehran claimed to be in the stronger position, the US has said it would ramp up sanctions to heap pressure on Tehran.

The American plan drew condemnation from Iran’s foreign ministry, which accused the US of “economic terrorism” and “crimes against humanity”.

“The perpetrators and instigators of these sanctions are deserving of trial and punishment for committing such heinous crimes,” it said in a statement carried by state media.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Thursday vowed Washington would “collapse” the Iranian regime with its threatened campaign nearly six months since their war began.

The comments underscored how the Trump administration is shifting to economic rather than military pressure on Tehran as the US president’s unpopular war drags on.

China also criticised Washington’s economic plan, saying that US “sanctions and pressure” would not resolve the Middle East conflict.

– ‘Economic D-Day’ –

Washington had urged other governments including Beijing to join efforts to isolate the Iranian economy.

Asked about US President Donald Trump’s threats, Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian told reporters on Friday that “sanctions and pressure will not help resolve the issue”.

“China calls on all relevant parties to take responsible measures and resolve the problem through political and diplomatic means,” he said.

Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to visit the White House on September 24 when the topic of Iran is sure to come up, as it did when Trump travelled to Beijing for a summit in May.

Bessent said the plan to ramp up economic sanctions against Iran meant Washington was less likely to have to return to heavy military operations against the country.

The US Treasury chief said he would give further details of the economic measures against Iran during a press conference on Monday.

Other senior Iranian officials also criticised the US sanctions plan.

“The so-called ‘Economic D-Day’ is a diversion from America’s own crisis: unprecedented debt & surging interest costs,” Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a post on X.

World.title: China, Indonesia hold talks on security, defence
World.content:
Jakarta – China’s foreign and defence ministers met their Indonesian counterparts in Jakarta Friday for talks seeking greater political and military cooperation days after a joint navy drill Taiwan blasted as a “provocation”.

The talks marked “an important milestone in our bilateral relations”, Indonesia’s foreign minister Sugiono, who goes by one name, said as he welcomed his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi.

“It serves as a forward-looking strategic platform, guiding our bilateral partnership across all five pillars — political, economic, maritime, people-to-people, and security.”

Indonesia maintains a neutral foreign policy, what it calls “free and active” — walking a diplomatic tightrope between Beijing and Washington.

Jakarta and Beijing raised the ire of Taiwan earlier this month with a joint navy drill off the democratic island’s east coast.

The two countries said it was a “passing exercise” with an Indonesian frigate passing through on its return home from the Russian port city of Vladivostok.

Taiwan called it a “military provocation” from the Chinese Communist Party.

Wang said Friday it was crucial for Beijing and Jakarta to “increase strategic communication, to deepen strategic coordination” as important representatives of the Global South.

“Today’s world is fluid and turbulent,” he said in translated remarks provided by Indonesia’s foreign ministry.

“We are seeing unilateralism and hegemonism. They have dealt a heavy blow to this world as well as to the global development agenda.”

– Missile factories –

The ministers on Friday headed the inaugural meeting of what is being called a “China-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism”.

Its purpose is to boost “the alignment of development strategies”, Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian told reporters ahead of Wang’s visit.

Wang was later joined by Chinese Defence Minister Dong Jun in talks with Indonesian counterparts on “political security and defence cooperation and international and regional situations”, according to Beijing.

Indonesian Defence Minister Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin later said the countries would “cooperate in missiles, rockets, and so on”, without giving further details.

“They (China) will help and they will transfer their technology so that we can build factories together in Indonesia,” he said.

Sjafrie said Jakarta and Beijing will also hold another military exercise this year under Heping Garuda, a recurring joint drill focused on humanitarian assistance, disaster relief and military-to-military cooperation.

Last year, Indonesia joined the BRICS bloc of emerging economies that includes Russia and China.

But President Prabowo Subianto has also signed a trade deal with US President Donald Trump and joined his so-called “Board of Peace”.

International relations researcher Pieter Pandie of the CSIS think tank told AFP that Jakarta still leaned “much more” towards Washington than Beijing.

“From the security and defence side of things, the Indonesia-China relationship is still very much less developed… compared with Indonesia’s security cooperation with other Western and Asian partners,” he said.

“I wouldn’t look too much into whether or not (Friday’s meeting) signals some sort of ‘realignment’ for Indonesia towards Beijing,” added Pandie.

World.title: 2,500 dead and rising — UN says DR Congo Ebola outbreak ‘growing exponentially’
World.content:
Geneva – The Ebola outbreak raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo is growing “exponentially”, with more than 2,500 deaths recorded and half of those in the last 20 days, the senior UN coordinator on the disease said Friday.

The Ebola outbreak is already the biggest in the country’s history and is spreading faster than any outbreak of the deadly virus on record.

According to the latest figures, the virus is “growing exponentially,” Julien Harneis told reporters in Geneva from Bunia, at the epicentre of the outbreak.

He said that in the last three months, “more than 2,500 people” had died, “and half of those in the last 20 days”.

“The epidemic is spreading widely. It’s now covering an area that is bigger than France…. It is growing faster and wider than the Ebola response.”

The DRC’s 17th Ebola outbreak is thought to have already been spreading for several weeks before it was officially declared on May 15.

It has hit regions in the north and east where the presence of the state is weak, health infrastructure is lacking and myriad armed groups have roamed for decades.

– ‘Alarming’ –

The Doctors Without Borders (MSF) charity also cautioned Friday that the outbreak was spreading “at an alarming rate”.

“This epidemic continues to spread, moving faster than the response can keep up,” MSF president Javid Abdelmoneim said in a statement.

Harneis stressed the need to ramp up the response, which has faced criticism for its slowness and poor organisation, and is also hampered by mistrust among the population.

Cases have so far been reported in six DRC provinces, including near the border with South Sudan, as well as in neighbouring Uganda.

Uganda, which saw two deaths from 20 Ebola cases, declared itself free of the virus last month.

There is no approved vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo virus strain behind the current surge, although a number of trials are underway.

And the World Health Organization said Thursday that the DRC would receive 70,000 doses of Ervebo vaccine, which has proved effective against the more common Zaire strain.

Earlier this month, WHO vaccine experts recommended a full-scale human trial of Ervebo, the only existing approved Ebola vaccine, to see if it offered cross-protection against the Bundibugyo strain.

Early data, notably from animal trials, has showed it may give some protection against Bundibugyo, but “it is not yet known whether Ervebo is protective against the Bundibugyo virus in humans”, WHO spokesman Christian Lindmeier stressed Friday.

– ‘Brutal’ –

Reining in the virus, which spreads by contact with bodily fluids and causes a haemorrhagic fever, has faced a multitude of other challenges.

Harneis highlighted the rampant insecurity and weak health system in eastern DRC.

“The law and order is undermined, and the basic services, particularly health, have been fragmented,” he said, describing the operating conditions as “brutal”.

Some 160 healthcare workers have fallen ill with Ebola since the start of the outbreak, including 43 who have died from the virus, he said, also pointing to repeated attacks on ambulance and other frontline workers.

Harneis also highlighted the barely functioning banking system, which has made it difficult get wages to those working on the outbreak, even as he said international funding cuts had reduced the capacity of humanitarian organisation by a third.

He called for more international support.

“If we provide more staffing, if we get more resources into remote areas across … the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo, within months we can slow the transmission and move to stopping it,” Harneis said.

“If we do not, … then this epidemic will become more deadly. It will spread wider and it risks to spread into neighbouring countries.”

World.title: Stocks tread cautiously as traders weigh US Treasury action
World.content:
London – Global stock markets traded cautiously on Friday as investors assessed the US Treasury’s effort to push down long-term borrowing costs, which spiked this week.

Oil prices held onto the week’s gains as the United States and Iran remained deadlocked over a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Bitcoin rallied and the dollar fell as the initial boost from the US Treasury’s surprise move to buy back more of its own bonds faded at the end of the week.

“The turmoil in the debt markets continues despite efforts to calm feverish borrowing costs,” said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.

“Investors remain concerned about inflationary risks and the growing mountain of government borrowing, while at the same time, debt being issued by tech giants building out the AI revolution is offering stiff competition,” she added.

The US Treasury’s action came after the 30-year yield surged to levels last seen in 2007, just before the global financial crisis.

Bitcoin has surged more than 20 percent since Wednesday, with the US Treasury’s efforts to push yields lower helping to drive demand for riskier assets.

The rally in the world’s biggest cryptocurrency by market value was also spurred by US President Donald Trump urging lawmakers to pass crypto legislation that has stalled in the Senate.

In Europe, the London, Paris and Frankfurt stock markets were all slightly higher. US equity futures were higher in pre-market trading.

The increase in yields weighed on Wall Street Thursday, where all three main indexes fell as tech firms — which rely on debt to fund their huge investments — dropped.

“For now, investors are viewing the Treasury’s steps more as a band-aid than a structural solution to rising yields,” said Deutsche Bank’s Jim Reid.

However, several Asian markets enjoyed another healthy day, with tech-rich Seoul helped higher by a rally in chipmakers.

Samsung jumped 3.9 percent as reports said it was planning a shareholder return worth as much as $79 billion.

Hong Kong also rose, while Tokyo fell and Shanghai was flat.

On currency markets, the yen rose against the dollar after Japanese inflation picked up last month on higher oil prices caused by the Middle East crisis, giving the country’s central bank room to hike interest rates next month. The euro also gained on the dollar.

Traders will be closely watching next week’s annual meeting of central bankers, economists and finance chiefs in Jackson Hole, hoping for some clarification on monetary policy.

World.title: Australia charges man with trying to pass Ukraine military intel to Russia
World.content:
Sydney – Australian police charged a man with foreign interference on Friday for allegedly seeking to pass intelligence about Ukrainian military activities to Russia.

The 27-year-old Russian-Australian citizen underwent “military-style” training in Russia and later joined the Ukrainian armed forces, Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett told a news conference.

Police allege he travelled to Russia for the training in October 2024 before returning to Australia, where he “maintained contact” with individuals he believed were linked to Moscow’s intelligence services.

He travelled in 2025 to Ukraine, where he enlisted in the country’s armed forces and “gained access to information relating to their military personnel, units and locations”, police allege.

Barrett said he then “provided, or attempted to provide, information obtained in Ukraine to individuals he believed were acting on behalf of Russian intelligence services”.

“It is alleged this conduct created a risk to the safety and security of Ukrainian military personnel,” she said.

“We don’t want Australia to become a safe haven for people who are undertaking foreign interference on behalf of other countries,” Barrett said.

A number of search warrants have been executed and it is a “possibility” there could be further arrests related to the case, she said.

The man was scheduled to face charges at a court hearing in Brisbane on Friday.

He has not been identified and was unemployed, Barrett said.

The investigation was conducted by federal police and the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO) spy agency.

“This case should put regimes perpetrating foreign interference on notice: we have zero tolerance,” ASIO Deputy Director-General Claire McGuinness said.

– ‘Aggression’ –

Ukraine’s ambassador to Australia called the case “deeply concerning” and said it was a “reminder that Russia’s aggression against Ukraine is not confined to the battlefield”.

“Standing with Ukraine also means understanding the nature of the threat posed by the Russian regime and remaining vigilant against its activities here in Australia,” Ambassador Vasyl Myroshnychenko told AFP.

“Russia is an Asia-Pacific nation and Australia has much to lose if Russia wins its illegal war of territorial annexation against Ukraine.”

In an email to AFP, Russia’s embassy in Canberra said it had learned of the case through media reports.

“At this stage, no official requests or notifications have been received by the Embassy or the Consulate General in Sydney, either from the Australian authorities or from the individual concerned,” the embassy said.

“We are currently using the available channels and resources to establish the circumstances of the case.”

It marks the eighth charging of an individual with crimes related to spying and foreign interference in Australia.

The crime of intentional foreign interference carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment in Australia.

Australia’s spy chief Mike Burgess singled out Russia last year as an “aggressive espionage threat” to the country.

In 2024, Australian police charged a married Russian-born couple with spying for Moscow, accusing them of accessing national security-related material from the military.

The 40-year-old woman, Kira Korolev, and her 62-year-old husband Igor — both holders of Russian passports — had lived in Australia for more than 10 years and had obtained citizenship, the authorities said.

World.title: Premier League returns with Arsenal eyeing title dynasty
World.content:
London – Champions Arsenal kick off the Premier League season on Friday reinforced by astute signings as boss Mikel Arteta welcomes the pressure of being “hunted” by their title rivals.

Just 34 days after a captivating World Cup came to an end, the Premier League returns, with Arsenal facing newly promoted Coventry at the start of their bid for a second successive title.

The Gunners have the honour of playing the opening game of the season at the Emirates Stadium, before a packed slate of top-flight matches across Saturday, Sunday and Monday.

Mohamed Salah and Pep Guardiola — two of the most iconic figures in Premier League history — have left Liverpool and Manchester City respectively.

But the Premier League remains packed with world-class talent and emerging stars.

Arsenal are the cream of the crop after winning the title for the first time in 22 years last season.

Installed as the bookmakers’ title favourites this term, Arsenal look well placed to reign supreme again, especially given the questions surrounding their title challengers.

They routed City 3-0 in the Community Shield last weekend to send a statement of intent to the chasing pack.

Bolstered by new signings Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis, with Ezri Konsa set to join from Aston Villa, Arteta has no doubts Arsenal can cope with the pressure of being the team everyone wants to beat.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” the Spaniard said.

“We need to show that desire, and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.

“If you give me the choice, I want to be first, I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Winning the Premier League was a cathartic moment for the north London club after so many near-misses raised doubts about their character.

– ‘A long marathon’ –

Arteta believes surviving that test of resolve will stand Arsenal in good stead as they bid to win back-to-back titles for the first time since the 1930s.

“We need to breathe because it’s going to be a long marathon,” he said.

“We have the ability to improve, to evolve, and that’s what I sense and I feel around the club, especially around the players.”

City, runners-up last season, start life without Guardiola at home to Bournemouth on Sunday.

Guardiola stepped down at the end of last season after winning 20 trophies in a glorious decade at the Etihad Stadium.

Former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca has accepted the daunting task of emulating the Spaniard’s success.

Liverpool’s new manager Andoni Iraola will take charge of his first game in Sunday’s trip to Newcastle, starting a new era without Egypt forward Salah after his move to Turkish club Trabzonspor.

Ex-Bournemouth boss Iraola was hired by Liverpool to replace Arne Slot, who was sacked following the Reds’ disappointing fifth-place finish last season.

Xabi Alonso begins his reign as Chelsea boss with a west London derby at Fulham on Monday.

Alonso, sacked by Real Madrid after less than eight months in charge last term, and Chelsea’s underachieving but expensively-assembled team, who finished a dismal 10th last term, have a point to prove this season.

“We feel ready. The desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building, looking forward to it,” Alonso said.

Manchester United start on Saturday at promoted Hull, who are back in the top tier for the first time since 2017.

United boss Michael Carrick has signed Belgium World Cup midfielder Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa and Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, with a deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in the pipeline.

Big-spending Tottenham, who narrowly avoided relegation last season, travel to Brentford on Saturday with two players signed for around 100 million pounds ($136.5 million) each — Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes — now in their ranks.

Europa League winners Villa, ravaged by a host of departures since last season, head to Brighton on Sunday.

World.title: Spurs agree deal to sign Man City’s Savinho: reports
World.content:
London – Tottenham have agreed a deal to sign Manchester City winger Savinho for an initial fee of around £75 million ($102 million), according to reports on Friday.

Savinho has been a long-term target for Tottenham, who failed in their attempt to sign the Brazil international during the 2025-26 campaign.

The 22-year-old Brazilian appears set to finally move to the north London club, who will pay an extra £10 million in potential add-ons.

Tottenham are also interested in signing Savinho’s City team-mate Omar Marmoush after the Egypt forward’s underwhelming spell in Manchester.

Savinho’s arrival will take Tottenham’s close-season spending beyond £300 million as boss Roberto De Zerbi rebuilds a squad that narrowly avoided relegation last season.

James Maddison, Dejan Kulusevski, Mohammed Kudus, Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are all either working their way back to fitness after injuries or still sidelined.

Those fitness issues mean Savinho should go straight into the Tottenham starting line-up if the deal is concluded in time for Saturday’s trip to Brentford in their first game of the Premier League season.

Savinho struggled to secure a regular starting berth at City, scoring seven goals, along with 16 assists, in 84 appearances.

World.title: Iraq PM Al-Zaidi says he will not seek second term
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has announced that he would not seek a second term, stating that his administration is focused on implementing long-term economic and institutional changes rather than staying in office.

Al-Zaidi said that he has personally vowed not to run again and that the changes implemented by his government would yield dividends for future governments.

His declaration occurred after a wide-ranging discussion of Iraq’s economy, oil exports, corruption, power, investment, and attempts to put weaponry completely under state control.

Despite recent financial pressures, the prime minister said that his government had met public-sector wages and government responsibilities.

Baghdad is also developing a budget that prioritizes power production, transmission, and distribution, as well as increased usage of solar energy.

Meanwhile, Iraq is stepping up attempts to diversify its oil shipments after recent regional interruptions that highlighted the country’s reliance on the Strait of Hormuz.

According to Al-Zaidi, Baghdad wants to increase exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan port while also investigating prospective routes through Syria’s Baniyas and Jordan’s Aqaba.

He also set an ambitious goal of increasing Iraqi oil output to 8-10 million barrels per day within six years, while advocating for a higher OPEC allocation that reflects Iraq’s populatioand its massiveve petroleum reserves.

On security, Al-Zaidi said that political groups believe that firearms must eventually be confined to the state and that methods are being devised for armed factions to relinquish their weapons.

He ruled out a military confrontation, but cautioned that uncontrolled weapons discourage investment and harm Iraq’s interests.

The prime minister also said that there will be no retreat from the government’s anti-corruption drive.

Baghdad is increasing its examination of government contracts before signing them, primarily to avoid inflated project prices and abuse of public funds.

Economic change will also need Iraq to reduce its reliance on government employment.

Al-Zaidi said that the government intends to boost the private sector and provide incentives for Iraqis to transition from public to private work.

His administration is also planning a scheme to provide one million residential land plots to Iraqis who do not currently own a house or residential land, with the initiative set to be finished in three years.

Regionally, Al-Zaidi said that Iraq cannot isolate itself from its Arab and regional neighbors and aims to turn the nation from a war zone into a bridge for discourse and economic cooperation.

But his most direct political statement concerns his destiny.

Al-Zaidi said that he does not plan to construct another administration around himself but rather to leave behind reforms that may continue after his departure, making the success of his premiership contingent not on a second term but on whether those improvements endure.

World.title: 'World looking at India as bright spot of growth & hope': PM Modi at Economic Times World Leaders Forum 2026
World.content:
From 'production-linked punishment' to PLI

'Prohibited unless permitted' to 'permitted unless prohibited'

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said the world is looking at India as a "bright spot of growth and hope", stressing that the country's reform journey has shifted from a "punishment model" under the earlier licence raj governments to an incentive-based approach.Addressing the Economic Times World Leaders Forum 2026, PM Modi said the world had witnessed several ups and downs in recent years and that the future of all nations was interconnected."The world has witnessed many ups and downs over the past few years, and these experiences have made one thing abundantly clear: whether one likes it or not, the futures of all nations are interconnected. Nothing is possible in isolation," the Prime Minister said."'One Earth, One Family, One Future' was India's guiding mantra during its G20 presidency. This spirit of a shared future, along with the accompanying sense of responsibility, offers solutions to many of the challenges facing the 21st-century world. There are various concerns regarding global growth. The world has witnessed a grim scenario recently; resources are being weaponized, and an atmosphere of mistrust is giving rise to numerous new challenges.Yet, even in such times, the world views India as a bright spot of growth and hope," he added.PM Modi criticised the earlier licence raj governments, saying they followed a "Production Linked Punishment" (PLP) model that penalised companies for increasing production.âTodayâs younger generation will be surprised to hear that there was a time in our country when if a company produced more than the prescribed limit, it was punished. This was the PLP, or Production Linked Punishment, model of the earlier licence raj governments,â he said.âThose who make fun of the Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat campaigns today are rooted in the same thinking of the past â PLP, or Production Linked Punishment,â he said.PM Modi also said the government is changing the country's regulatory philosophy by moving away from the earlier approach of requiring permission for activities unless explicitly allowed.âEarlier, the approach to regulations was âprohibited unless permittedâ â meaning you could not do something unless the government gave you permission. We are changing this approach to âpermitted unless prohibitedâ. That means, for anything that is not explicitly prohibited by law, there should be no need to seek permission at every step.âHe said the shift was intended to recast the relationship between the state, citizens and businesses around trust rather than suspicion.âThe relationship between the government and citizens should be based not on suspicion, but on trust,â PM Modi added.The Prime Minister also highlighted legislative work undertaken during the Monsoon Session of Parliament."In the Monsoon Session of Parliament, we have passed the Bankersâ Books Evidence Bill, even as the Opposition has continued to create disruptions in Parliament. We did not allow the work of serving the country to stop," he said."We are not just changing regulations, we are changing entire policy of regulations," PM Modi said at the ET Global Leaders' Forum.Speaking ahead of PM Modi's keynote address at the summit, Times Internet chairman Satyan Gajwani said Modi had emerged as a source of stability in a world "lurching from one crisis to the next."Gajwani said the global landscape was being reshaped by multiple, overlapping disruptions - two ongoing wars, an energy crisis, disrupted shipping routes, trade wars and the rapid AI revolution - creating unprecedented uncertainty for governments, businesses and economies.He said India's political and economic stability, coupled with its growth and reform trajectory, had positioned the country as a reliable force amid growing geopolitical uncertainty.Gajwani said PM Modi's leadership and policy continuity had helped provide businesses and investors with greater predictability, while giving India an opportunity to play a larger role in the evolving global order.

World.title: Crowd-funded anti-bribery portal shuts after amassing 2 lakh users in 48 hrs
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bribes.fyi began as a side project and, within 48 hours, clocked 5 million requests and 2 lakh new users. It shut down as suddenly as its meteoric rise took social media by surprise.Built by 20-year-old Delhi BTech student Aryan Nishad, it displayed a neon-red map of India for anonymous reports of alleged bribe demands. By Aug 17, it had logged reports from 253 citiesâagainst police, RTOs, and revenue and land records offices, and passport offices. 37% were, interestingly, marked ârefusedâ, meaning users said they did not pay and still got their work done. The site stressed these were user submissions, not verified cases.The site then abruptly went offline, citing traffic, data security, spam, duplicate entries and misuse. Calling the shutdown voluntary and precautionary, the team said: âWhat we did not build was the infrastructure to carry that kind of attention safelyâ. They acknowledged it was ânot the right custodian for it at that scaleâ.In their farewell note, they said: "Shutting it down was our decision. It was always meant to send a signal, not point fingers.I think the signal was sent."The website and the traction it got from the public has generated huge conversation, with lawyers and experts weighing in. Section 8 of the Prevention of Corruption Act criminalises giving or promising an undue advantage to a public servant, punishable with up to seven yearsâ imprisonment after a 2018 amendment. An exception applies to someone compelled to pay who reports the demand within seven days. But a public admission on a website falls outside that protection.âSo a person writing, âI paid Rs 5,000 to get my licence issuedâ may be making a statement potentially relevant to their own criminal liability,â said Mishi Choudhary, technology lawyer and founder of Software Freedom Law Center (SFLC.in). The law has a policy problem, she said, and platforms must build âanonymity and security by design... from the beginningâ and ânot collect identity at allâ.The safest approach, she said, is to collect minimum data because complainants âcanât be punished twice for doing what the system is forcing them to doâ. Such a service is âa repository of sensitive personal data, allegations of criminal conduct and police informationâ, she added.The platform also raises intermediary-liability questions because it collected, moderated, categorised and mapped allegations instead of merely hosting them.âSafe harbour under Section 79 protects an intermediary that does not select or modify the information it hosts,â said Apar Gupta, founder director of Internet Freedom Foundation. âModerating and approving reports... is an active functionâ that may exceed that role, he said, citing ongoing Wikipedia litigation in Delhi. Under Shreya Singhal vs Union of India 2015, removal requires a court order or govt notification, not a private complaint, though IT Rules prescribe grievance timelines. âA disclaimer offers no protection by itself.â Officials, he said, âcomplain to the police, not to the courts.âPlatforms collecting names, phone numbers or IP addresses are data fiduciaries under the DPDP Act and face penalties up to Rs 250 crore for security failures, though Section 17 exempts govt agencies. âA platform cannot promise anonymity while retaining identifying records,â Gupta said. Data must be handed over within 72 hours of an authorised request, while disproportionate demands can be challenged under Puttaswamy.Yet âthere is little protection for complainantsâ. Gupta cited a Lokniti-CSDS survey finding nearly two-thirds fear legal action for online speech. The Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 was never operationalised.For a relaunch, Gupta recommended no accounts, no IP logs, stripped metadata, aggregate figures instead of names, referrals to newsrooms, a grievance officer and transparency reports. âDecentralisation is not a legal defence,â he said, noting BitChat and GitHub were blocked during Julyâs Delhi protests.

World.title: Jharkhand protest: Scuffle breaks out between students, police over burning Hemant Soren's effigy
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A scuffle broke out in Ranchi between student protesters and police following an attempt to burn effigies of Jharkhand chief minister

and Congress leader

.

âThey gathered in large numbers at the prominent Albert Chowk to burn effigies of CM Soren and Rahul Gandhi.

When the police tried to control them, a scuffle broke out. JMM workers were also present at the spot,â an official told news agency PTI.

This comes a day after the Jharkhand high court stayed the government's decision to cancel public recruitment examinations after irregularities were flagged.

In a social media post on X, Bharatiya Janata Party shared a video of the scuffle and accused "JMM and Congress goons" of attacking the protesters in the presence of police.

"It is extremely unfortunate that students en route to a peaceful effigy burning in Ranchi were attacked by JMM and Congress goons in the presence of the police, and this constitutes an attempt to murder democracy," BJP's Jharkhand unit said.

"Even little girls were not spared; in the absence of female police personnel, brutality was inflicted upon them by JMM goons and the police," it added.

The Jharkhand High Court on August 20 stayed the state government's order cancelling the appointment of government employees recruited through the 11th to 13th JPSC examinations.





On August 18, the Jharkhand government had issued a notification cancelling 22 recruitment examinations, including the 11th to 13th JPSC examinations, after weeks of public protests over alleged irregularities.

The court's order came while hearing various petitions filed by the newly appointed officers against the government's decision.

This has hurt the students and the general public of the state."

World.title: ‘Received no help’: Odisha man’s body kept on rooftop for 18 hours amid floods
World.content:
Odisha flood water

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

'Received no help from administration'

NEW DELHI: The body of a 61-year-old man in Odishaâs Jajpur district remained on the rooftop of his flooded home for nearly 18 hours as rising waters prevented his family from bringing him down for his last rites, relatives said on Friday.The incident took place in Chintasahi under Bari panchayat, where several families have remained surrounded by floodwaters for six days following the swelling of the Brahmani and Kharasrota rivers.The deceased, Hrushikesh Mallik, died around 4.30pm on Wednesday. With nearly four feet of water inundating the ground floor of the house, his family kept his body on the rooftop until the water receded on Thursday.News agency PTI reported that relatives repeatedly sought help from the local administration to take the body out for the last rites but received no assistance.âWe repeatedly called the Bari Block Development Officer (BDO) for administrative assistance for the last rites of my uncle, but the calls were not answered,â said Anil Mallik, the deceasedâs nephew.He said the family then approached a powerboat operator involved in rescue operations, but the operator told them he could not reach the village without instructions from senior authorities.A local social worker eventually arranged a hearse. Villagers carried the body through waist-deep water for nearly a kilometre as the road from the house remained submerged.The incident has sparked anger among residents, who alleged that hundreds of families in Chintasahi have been forced to remain on rooftops for the past six days with limited access to food.

World.title: 'No use of cockroach inside house': BJP mocks CJP after team 'attacked' during Rajasthan school visit
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party's attempt to inspect a government school in Rajasthan triggered a political storm after party members alleged they were attacked while trying to visit a school they claimed had been operating from a buffalo shed for years.

"BJP goons have once again resorted to violence against our team. The BJP is fine with children continuing to study in a buffalo shed, but if we try to get these schools fixed, that is not acceptable to them," CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka posted on X.

The confrontation took place in Kanvarpura village in Jaipur district's Bagru Assembly constituency, where a CJP delegation had travelled to inspect the school's condition.

Videos shared by CJP showed a scuffle breaking out between members of the delegation and a group of men near the village, with stones allegedly thrown at their vehicle, damaging its rear windshield. The party claimed around 40 members were injured and taken to a hospital in Jaipur.

Ranka later alleged the attack was carried out at the behest of Rajasthan education minister Madan Dilawar. "The school will be fixed, one way or another," CJP said.





BJP MLA Gopal Sharma mocked the party, saying: "What is CJP? There is no use of a cockroach inside a house. Children and youth belong in a house."

Rajasthan junior home minister Jawahar Singh Bedham alleged that Congress supporters were operating behind the CJP banner, while social justice minister Avinash Gehlot called the group "a party of anarchic elements."

World.title: 'His personal views': Punjab Congress distances itself from Deepender Hooda over Sajjan Kumar tribute row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Punjab Congress leaders on Friday sought to distance the party's state unit from Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda's remarks describing former party MP and 1984 anti-Sikh riots convict Sajjan Kumar as a "role model nationwide".

The leaders said the party stood with those who were killed and affected by the violence and that it was Hooda's "personal views".

The pushback from Punjab Congress came a day after Sajjan Singh Kumar, who was serving a life sentence in connection with the 1984 riots, died at the age of 84 at Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi.

Hooda had described Kumar's death as an "irreparable loss" to the country's political landscape and said he had been a prominent figure whose connect with people was "exemplary".

The remarks triggered sharp criticism from Sikh groups, opposition parties and families of riot victims, forcing Congress leaders in Punjab to clarify that Hooda's comments did not reflect their position.

'We stand with those who died'

Congress MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Kumar had committed "misdeeds", had been punished for them and could not be held up as a model for political leadership.

"Sajjan Kumar did misdeeds. He has been punished for his actions.





A leader does not lead in harming others. We stand with those who died due to him," Aujla said in Amritsar.

Asked specifically about Hooda's remarks, Aujla said they should be viewed as the Haryana MP's personal opinion.

"It must be the personal opinion of Hooda ji but our view is that whatever happened and whoever it happened with, we stand with them, the victims," he said.

Punjab Congress working president Raj Kumar Verka also sought to put the focus on the victims of the violence.

"Sajjan Kumar's life had been full of controversies. This is a matter related to Punjab and Punjabis have been hurt. If Sajjan Kumar is being held responsible for it, we first stand in support of those innocent people; Sajjan Kumar comes only later," Verka said.

"I don't know who said what. We are Punjabis and we will continue to stand with Punjabis," he added.

Congress MP Manish Tewari, however, declined to comment directly on Hooda's statement, saying he had not read it.

"I haven't read the statement, so it won't be correct to comment on it," Tewari said

What Deepender Hooda said

Hooda's comments came after Kumar's death on Thursday.

Speaking to ANI, Hooda described Kumar's death as a loss to the political landscape and praised his public connect.

"Today, the country's political landscape has suffered an irreparable loss... He is cited as a role model nationwide," Hooda had said.

The remarks quickly became controversial given Kumar's conviction in cases related to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, which followed the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi by her Sikh bodyguards.

Kumar was a three-time parliamentarian and had faced criminal proceedings over the violence for decades. His legal journey included both acquittals and convictions before higher courts.

BJP, SAD attack Congress

The BJP and

sharply criticised Hooda and questioned whether his remarks represented the Congress's broader position.

BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu accused Kumar and his associates of systematically targeting Sikh families during the 1984 violence and alleged that the Congress leadership had protected him for years.

Bittu called on the Punjab and Delhi Congress units to clarify their position on Hooda's comments.

The Shiromani Akali Dal also demanded an apology from Hooda and the Congress.

SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia condemned the statement and said Congress should apologise.

"How can a person like Jagdish Tytler, HKL Bhagat...and all those who killed our innocent Sikh brothers in broad daylight and are responsible for the murder of around 3,000 people during the 1984 riots, be called role models?" Majithia said.

He also questioned whether Hooda would continue to remain in the Congress after making the remarks.

SAD leader Daljeet Singh Cheema said Hooda should have considered the impact of his comments on families whose homes were destroyed and relatives killed during the violence.

"When you glorify the life of such people in public, it causes a great deal of hurt to the Sikh community," Cheema said.

The president of the 1984 Anti-Sikh Riots Victim Welfare Society, Surjit Singh, also condemned Hooda's remarks, saying victims had still not received justice.

Victims' family react to Sajjan Kumar's death

The controversy unfolded alongside emotional reactions from families affected by the 1984 violence.

Ganga Kaur, a member of a riot-affected family, said members of her family had been killed during the violence.

"Members of our family were burned alive in front of us. Sajjan Kumar died naturally, but we would have found greater peace if he had been executed," she told ANI.

Another victim-family member, who identified himself as Surjit Singh, said seven members of his family were burned alive during the riots.

"It is very unfortunate that Deepender Hooda is siding a criminal. He should be ashamed of praising a person who is responsible for the massacre of so many people," he said.

Sajjan Kumar died at Safdarjung Hospital on Thursday at the age of 84. Hospital authorities said he had a history of high blood pressure and Parkinson's disease and had been admitted after being brought to the hospital by police with altered sensorium.

Kumar had been serving a life sentence after the Delhi high court in December 2018 overturned his acquittal in the Raj Nagar case, relating to the killing of five members of a Sikh family and the burning of a gurdwara during the 1984 violence.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He surrendered and was lodged in Tihar Jail in December 2018.

In February 2025, a Delhi court sentenced Kumar to another life term in the Saraswati Vihar case over the killings of Jaswant Singh and his son Tarundeep Singh during the riots.

The court spared him the death penalty, citing his age, medical condition and conduct while serving his earlier sentence.

In another case relating to violence in Janakpuri and Vikaspuri, a Rouse Avenue court acquitted Kumar in January 2026 of charges linked to the killing of Sohan Singh and his son-in-law Avtar Singh and the burning of Gurcharan Singh. The Delhi high court subsequently issued notice on an appeal against the acquittal.

World.title: TGIIC auction fetches ₹264 crore per acre
World.content:
Underscoring Hyderabad’s emergence as one of India’s most dynamic real estate markets, plots auctioned by the Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) were sold at ₹264 crore per acre.

The TGIIC achieved a strong outcome through its e-auction of Plot No. P1 in Raidurg, generating ₹1,386 crore from 5.25 acres of prime multi-use land. Plot No. P1 (5.25 acres) was auctioned against a reserve price of ₹175 crore per acre - a 50.9% premium over the reserve price.

The auction also marks an increase from TGIIC’s previous Raidurg auction in May 2026, when land was sold at ₹237 crore per acre. The latest transaction has taken the price to ₹264 crore per acre.

The auction was conducted through the MSTC e-Auction platform, with JLL acting as the transaction advisor. The process saw participation from developers seeking land along Hyderabad’s business and infrastructure corridors.

Vice Chairman and Managing Director of TGIIC, K. Shashanka, said the auction result reflects the confidence of the developer community in Telangana’s development plans. He said the participation and competition during the process showed market interest in Hyderabad as a business destination.

World.title: Now, protesters at Jantar Mantar seek overhaul of reservation system
World.content:
Thousands of protesters gathered at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Friday (August 21, 2026) under the banner of Reservation Hatao Andolan (RHA), a CJP-style Instagram-page led mobilisation of anger against India’s reservation policy as it exists. The protesters called for an overhaul of the reservation system, demanding that quota in public education and employment solely be based on an income criteria rather than on socio-economic categories, and also raised demands like “one family, one reservation”, and called for the government to roll back the UGC’s 2026 caste-equity rules.

The movement began when a student, Harsh Dubey, started the RHA Instagram page while the student movement being led by the Cockroach Janta Party was demanding the resignation of erstwhile Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Soon after Mr. Pradhan’s resignation, Mr. Dubey said he had handed over control of the page to veteran anti-reservation and general category activists Anuradha Tiwari, Ajeet Bharti, and Neha Das.

The protests in Jantar Mantar on Friday (August 21) come amidst the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Union government reiterating India’s stance that reservations for socio-economic categories such as Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes were not a poverty alleviation scheme but a scheme meant to ensure the representation of marginalised communities that have suffered from social, economic, and educational backwardness for generations. Further, on Thursday (August 20), the Union government had told the Supreme Court that it was rethinking the 2026 UGC equity regulations, which had led to wave of protests in January this year as well.

On Friday (August 21) morning, the protesters, many of whom were mobilised by different organisations representing people from “general” castes such as Karni Sena and Ranbir Sena, arrived at Jantar Mantar despite public statements from the Delhi Police saying that no permission had been granted for a demonstration at this site. By noon on Friday (August 21), the Delhi Police released another statement saying the protest had been permitted but at Ramlila Ground.

Stand-off with police

However, the protesters, hundreds of whom had already gathered at Jantar Mantar, refused to leave and had a stand off with the security personnel guarding the Jantar Mantar protest site behind multiple layers of barricading. Around 2 p.m., even as protesters shouted slogans against reservation, chanted “UGC rollback”, blew conch shells and chanted ‘Jai Shree Ram’, security personnel opened the barricading, resulting in the protesters pouring into the Jantar Mantar site. By evening, the protesters had set up a stage with a banner that read: “Reservation Reform Satyagraha”.

The Delhi Police have not responded to questions about whether permission has been granted for the protest at Jantar Mantar site subsequently.

Around 7.30 p.m., police personnel announced on loudhailers that the gathering at Jantar Mantar had been declared illegal and security personnel could be seen putting protesters on buses and taking them away from the site. As the police took protesters away on the buses, they charged, “Jab jab Modi darta hai, police ko aage karta hai”, a slogan that was recently popularised during the police action on students marching to Parliament.

The Delhi Police have not yet responded to The Hindu’s queries on how many protesters were detained.

However, Ms. Tiwari told The Hindu late on Friday, “The protest will continue. More people are coming. The police cannot act like this. They did the same thing during the Cockroach protest as well.”

Alok Pratap Singh from Bihar’s Ranbir Sena told The Hindu, “There is a huge problem in the way we have let reservation system take over every aspect of politics. It has led to people seeing the General category folks in a certain way. Poverty does not have caste and there is no reason to continue with reservation for certain caste groups. We are at a point where all caste groups are equal. So, now our demand is that reservation should be based only on income and not on caste categories.”

Himani Sisodia, 27, from Uttar Pradesh’s Saharanpur, had also arrived at the protest site, and said, “General caste people like us are the ones who are suffering because of reservations. We are paying double the price for entrance exam forms, we are getting more marks in the examinations and yet we are losing jobs to reserved categories who are paying less to register and getting fewer marks. This has happened to me also and that is why I am here today.”

To submit memo to govt.

Ms. Tiwari, who has been part of the team handling the RHA page, said the movement would be submitting an official letter to the government with their demands shortly and added that for the time being the demands were focused on reforming the reservation policy. “This has become an untouchable topic. Nobody is willing to talk about the need to reform the reservation system,” she said.

A significant argument that the RHA movement has been making to support its call for overhauling the reservation system has been to point towards the concentration of quotas being availed by a small section of communities within each category of SC, ST, and OBC. This argument, which has led to larger calls for maybe introducing a creamy layer concept or the tool of sub-categorisation, is being used by the RHA movement to call for an overhaul of the system itself.

On the Instagram page, the RHA has posted a total of five demands. These are: income-based reservation; one family, one reservation — arguing reservation should only be available for one generation of a family; minimum qualifying marks for examinations and de-reserving unfilled reserved seats; a freeze on the 50% cap on reservations, a ban on political parties promising increased reservation, and periodic review of lists of communities that can qualify for quotas; and a sunset clause that provides an end date for reservations.

But even as the protesters gathered at Jantar Mantar throughout Friday (August 21), the activists leading the RHA page have not yet made a statement about how long they intend to demonstrate. While Ms. Tiwari insisted that there is no leadership to the protest as it was an “organic movement of the general category”, Abhishek Agnihotri, one of the protesters who had sought permission from the Delhi Police, said the protest was intended to “keep going”.

World.title: ‘Kallan Vijayan’ row: former editor in-charge of Deshabhimani weekend supplement resigns
World.content:
Journalist K.R. Ajayan, who was till recently the editor in-charge of Deshabhimani’s weekend supplement, has resigned, weeks after a headline with the words ‘Kallan Vijayan’ (Vijayan, the thief) in it allegedly sparked an internal row.

Mr. Ajayan said he put in his papers on Friday after meeting the General Manager of Deshabhimani, the CPI(M) mouthpiece, and on being given the assurance that his service benefits would not be affected.

At the centre of the controversy was the headline ‘Kallan Vijayan, Dhanya Natakagramam, Muthippara P.O.,’ given to a feature article planned in July on a veteran theatre artiste from Muthippara in Thiruvananthapuram district. Following objections to the headline, the supplement was allegedly published later after replacing the article in question.

Mr. Ajayan, meanwhile, had reportedly been asked to give an explanation, which he says he did. He had stood by his choice of headline, and, subsequently, was relieved of his duties. Journalist T.C. Rajesh, who wrote the article, later published it on his Facebook page.

The allegedly censored piece had put the CPI(M) in a spot, with its Resident Editor M. Swaraj blaming the non-publication of the periodical supplement on July 19 on a “technical error”.

World.title: PNGRB authorises about 1,800 km LPG pipeline infra with ₹7,000 crore capital investment
World.content:
The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) informed on Friday (August 21, 2026) that it has given its green light for the development of approximately 1,800 km of pipeline infrastructure for transporting Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG).

Spanning across six States — Telangana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Karnataka and Goa — they are estimated to involve a capital investment of approximately ₹7,000 crore.

The pipelines sanctioned include that from Cherlapally (Telangana) to Nagpur (Maharashtra) which is a distance of 556 km, from Jhansi (Uttar Pradesh) to Sitarganj (Uttarakhand) which runs approximately 611 km, and 633 km from Shikrapur (Maharashtra) to Goa & Hubli (Karnataka) Pipeline. State-owned gas distributor GAIL (India) Limited would be developing these projects.

Upon completion, the latest-ratified pipelines are expected to augment the country’s overall LPG network by about 24% from about 7,700 km to about 9,500 km.

Major portion of India’s LPG imports are brought in via coastal locations and then are hauled across to other parts of the country.

“These projects will substantially reduce the movement of LPG tank trucks, thereby improving road safety, lowering logistics costs, reducing traffic congestion and significantly decreasing carbon emissions through a modal shift from road to pipelines,” the regulator stated.

It added that as the country continues to rely significantly on imported LPG, the extensive network would help impart “inherent system resilience”.

World.title: Rangasamy draws flak for not attending Southern Zonal Council meeting
World.content:
Chief Minister and AINRC founder N. Rangasamy has come under criticism for his decision not to attend the Southern Zonal Council meeting held at Mamallapuram on Thursday.

In a video message, former Chief Minister and Congress leader V. Narayanasamy said Mr. Rangasamy with his decision to skip an important meeting chaired by the Union Home Minister Amit Shah has done “injustice” to the people of Puducherry.

The Southern Zonal Council meeting is an important forum for States and Union Territories to raise issues before the Central government. The Puducherry government was represented by Lieutenant Governor K. Kailashnathan at Thursday’s meeting. The Lt. Governor’s address at the meeting was limited to outlining the Union Territory’s plans towards addressing the water problem, the Congress leader said.

“There are many other problems faced by Puducherry and those issues could only be raised by the Chief Minister. Mr. Rangasamy often speaks on the need for Statehood, but he failed to use the platform of Southern Zonal Council meeting to raise the issue. His non-participation shows that the Chief Minister was not serious at all in getting Statehood for the region,” the former Chief Minister said.

Former Member of Parliament and president of Puducherry Maanila Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam M. Ramadass in a statement said the absence of the Chief Minister merely because the Lt. Governor was participating was not acceptable in the Union Territory’s scheme of administration.

The demand for Statehood has been pending for more than 50 years. The Chief Minister could have raised the issue strongly by participating in the meeting. Both the Chief Minister and the Lt. Governor could have attended and presented their respective Constitutional and administrative perspectives on issues concerning Puducherry, he said.

“As the head of an elected government, the Chief Minister could have only strongly articulated the Statehood demand. The Lt. Governor cannot be expected to champion such a political demand. The Chief Minister has a responsibility to utilise every available opportunity to safeguard and advance the interests of Puducherry. The Lt. Governor and the Chief Minister should work together for the development of the Union Territory,” the former MP said.

World.title: Two men arrested in Coimbatore for possession of 2,100 prescription tablets
World.content:
The Selvapuram police in Coimbatore on Friday arrested two persons on charge of possessing 2,100 prescription tablets, which were meant to be sold in the black market.

According to the police, they had arrested Sarbudheen (35) for selling prescription tablets some days ago. He revealed to the police that Manikandan (26) from Perur sold him the tablets. Manikandan was under the surveillance of the police after the incident.

The police intercepted Manikandan and his friend Sakthivel (27) during a patrol on Friday after finding them moving in a suspicious manner. The police frisked them and found that they were carrying 2,100 prescription tablets. They were arrested.

World.title: CJP activists assaulted in Rajasthan village during school inspection attempt
World.content:
A team of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists was allegedly assaulted and chased out of Rampura-Kanwarpura village near Jaipur on Friday (August 21, 2026), when it made an attempt to inspect a government school as part of the organisation’s ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign. The vehicles of team members were damaged and women supporters were allegedly roughed up.

The CJP activists, led by party co-convener Ashutosh Ranka, had travelled to the village, situated in Bagru Assembly constituency, to inspect the Government Primary School and interact with the students and teachers. However, some villagers had barricaded the approach road and checked the vehicles entering the area.

When the team of about 40 CJP workers arrived in the village, some people confronted them, raised slogans, and asked them to leave. During a scuffle that followed, the team members were allegedly manhandled and driven out with stone-pelting. The villagers later staged a sit-in outside the school.

‘BJP involved’

Mr. Ranka said one volunteer had suffered a fractured arm. He alleged that those involved in the attack had been brought in by the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party. “We had informed the police about our visit to Rampura-Kanwarpura. The police were aware of stone-pelting in the area but did not intervene,” he told journalists after leaving the village.

The school building had earlier been declared unsafe because of its dilapidated condition and closed. Currently, classes for students are being held in a cattle enclosure close to the building. “We had inspected the school last year as well… It was being run in a buffalo shed even then,” Mr. Ranka said.

The villagers, however, claimed that the funds for school repair work had already been sanctioned.

Agitation threatened

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced that he would arrive in Jaipur and launch an agitation if the school repair work did not begin, and if the BJP members who allegedly attacked CJP volunteers were not arrested within the next 48 hours.

The CJP, which cancelled its visit to another government school in a nearby village later in the day, claimed that the confrontation in Rampura-Kanwarpura was pre-planned and had the backing of State Education Minister Madan Dilawar.

‘Political battlegrounds’

The confrontation occurred amid a political row over a recent Education Department order imposing restrictions on the entry of outsiders into government schools and barring photography and videography without the written approval of the heads of institutions. The order was issued after CJP activists joined an agitation by students and villagers at a school in Alwar district on August 14.

The CJP has opposed the restriction and accused the BJP government of attempting to prevent public scrutiny of the condition of government schools. The party’s ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign seeks to assess the condition of school buildings, availability of teachers, and other facilities and academic arrangements.

The incident also spilled over into the Rajasthan Assembly, where the BJP and the Opposition Congress traded allegations. Education Minister Mr. Dilawar later accused the CJP and Congress of attempting to “disrupt education and spoil the atmosphere”. He added: “Turning the schools into political battlegrounds is extremely regrettable. Everyone should remain vigilant against the attempts to tarnish the school environment for selfish interests.”

The People’s Union for Civil Liberties-Rajasthan demanded the immediate arrest of all those accused of attacking the CJP delegation. He also sought an impartial inquiry into the failure of police officials to take preventive action despite receiving prior information about the possibility of an attack.

World.title: Muthanga violence: Kerala High Court suspends sentence of Geethanandan, three others
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has suspended the sentence of four persons convicted for the violence associated with the police action to evict tribal community protesters from the Muthanga wildlife sanctuary, Wayanad, in 2003.

The court further ordered that they be released on bail. A Bench of Justice A. Badharudeen passed the order on appeals filed by the convicts, challenging their conviction and sentence by the Principal Session’s Court, Kalpetta, and seeking bail.

The High Court had earlier this month orally observed that the trial court ought to have done a thorough scrutiny and come up with a conclusive finding, rather than rely solely on prima facie evidence while convicting social activist M. Geethanandan and three others — Binu, Rameshan and Anilkumar — in connection with the alleged attempt to murder a senior civil police officer and the alleged abduction of a forest range officer, which was probed by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

The standing counsel for the CBI submitted that the agency too would file an appeal on the matter, to address the ‘flaws’ in the sessions court’s judgment.

‘Legally unsustainable’

The trial court had awarded five years’ rigorous imprisonment to the convicts and imposed a fine of ₹36,000. Terming their conviction legally unsustainable, the convicts contended that it was based on a finding by the trial court that there was prima facie a criminal conspiracy.

Two persons, a protester and a police officer, had been killed in police firing and allied violence in the land struggle. The trial court had acquitted the appellants of charges relating to the death of K.V. Vinod, the police constable, in the violence. The trial court had delivered its judgment on July 31, 23 years after the Muthanga land agitation.

Struggle for land

Armed police and forest officials had moved into the wildlife sanctuary, to evict hundreds of tribal families in 2003. The families had occupied the reserved forest land under the banner of the Adivasi Gothra Maha Sabha (AGMS), raising demands for equitable land distribution.

Out of the 57 persons accused, 15 had died before the trial’s conclusion. Asokan, the second accused and one of those who had died, had been found guilty of delivering the fatal blow to the police constable.

World.title: PTI slams govt for ‘flouting’ SC order, opp says it will approach SC over contempt
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Friday accused the government of committing contempt of court by “flouting” the Supreme Court’s order to shift incarcerated party founder Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital, and announced that it would approach the apex court on Saturday.

On Tuesday, the SC had directed the government to move Imran to Shifa International Hospital, a private facility. All eyes were on the hospital with a heavy police presence stationed on Thursday night. However, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar revealed on Friday that Imran was instead taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims).

It is worth mentioning that the SC had ordered that Imran’s medical reports or information concerning his health should not be used for political purposes.

On Friday, Imran’s sister Uzma Khan, who was present for his medical examination, addressed a press conference in Islamabad alongside his personal physician, Dr Faisal Sultan. She said they had received a phone call on Thursday to reach Adiala jail, where Imran is incarcerated.

“So we reached the Adiala jail at around 8-8:30pm,” she added. Uzma said they were then taken to a deputy superintendent of police’s room, whom she identified as Sibtain.

“Later, Sibtain sahib asked Dr Sultan to go outside the room with him and me to stay in the room. Then, after around 10 to 15 minutes, a female assistant sub-inspector took me to a car.”

She added that all this while, police did not answer any of her queries, including those about Dr Sultan. Uzma said she was then taken to Pims.

“I asked them why you have brought me here; the SC has instructed for (Imran’s) treatment at Shifa International Hospital. At that, they told me we were there for a follow-up regarding Imran’s eye.”

Imran has been taken to Pims for treatment multiple times after his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January.
